transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I’m here because I’ve gotten… really slowed down. Like, not just tired or procrastinating. At work I’ll open an audit workpaper and just sit there staring at it, and twenty minutes can go by before I even move my hand to type anything. I know what I’m supposed to do, or I think I do, but it’s like my body and my brain won’t start.

I’m an accountant, so I’m used to being careful and checking things, but this is different. It’s so slow that people at work have started noticing I’m not keeping up. That’s what finally made me come in, because I can’t really hide it anymore.
Have you noticed any changes in your mood or emotions lately, like feeling sad, hopeless, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy?

Yes… yeah, I have. Most days, honestly, I wake up and before I even open my eyes all the way, there’s this heavy, hollow feeling in my chest. It’s hard to describe without sounding dramatic, but it’s like the day already feels ruined before it’s even started. Like I’m already behind, or like there’s no point in trying to catch up because it’s all just going to feel the same.

It’s not just a bad mood that lifts once I get moving. It kind of sits there. I’ll lie there thinking, “I have to get up, I have to shower, I have to go to work,” but emotionally it feels like I’m dragging something around inside me. It’s this empty weight, if that makes sense. Like heavy and hollow at the same time.
How long have you been feeling this way?

About seven months now, I think. It kind of started around when my husband stopped working after his company downsized. At first I told myself it was just stress from that, like anyone would feel overwhelmed if the household suddenly changed like that, and I kept thinking, “Okay, once we adjust, I’ll feel normal again.”

But it didn’t really lift. Month after month it’s just been there, and I can look back now and see it’s been pretty steady since then. Seven months sounds strange to say out loud because I kept treating it like something temporary, but… yeah, about seven months.
Have you found that things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or time with friends or family, don’t bring you the same pleasure or satisfaction anymore?

Yes. That’s actually been one of the weirdest parts, because I used to have things that made me feel like myself. I used to plan hikes ahead of time, like look up trails and check the weather and pack snacks, and I’d bring my camera because I liked taking photos while I was out. Not professionally or anything, just… it made me happy to notice things.

And Sundays used to be my cooking day. I’d make something a little involved, or prep meals, put on music, kind of make a whole thing of it. I also volunteered at the library, and I really used to like that—helping people find things, shelving books, just being around that quiet kind of order.

Now all of that just feels like… items on a checklist. Like I can remember that I used to care about them, but I don’t feel the caring part. Even thinking about starting feels like too much effort, and if I force myself to do something, there’s not really any satisfaction in it. It’s more like, “Okay, I did the thing,” but there’s no reward feeling afterward.
Have you ever had periods where your mood was unusually high, or you felt more energetic or irritable than usual, even if others might not have noticed?

I don’t think so… not really. I mean, I’ve had normal days where I’m maybe a little more keyed up if there’s a deadline or if I’m irritated about something, but I wouldn’t say I’ve had periods where I felt unusually high or energized in that way.

If anything, I feel like I’ve been trying to remember if there was some stretch where I was suddenly myself again or more than myself, but nothing comes to mind. I don’t think anyone has ever said I seemed like I was acting unusually energetic or different, either. I guess I’m not totally sure what would count, but from how you’re describing it, no, I haven’t really noticed that.
Have you ever had a period where you felt this way for 2 years or more without a significant improvement in your mood?

No, not two years. It feels long, honestly, because being in it day after day makes seven months feel like… I don’t know, much longer than it sounds. But if I’m answering the question directly, it’s been about seven months, starting around when my husband stopped working after the downsizing.

Before that, I wouldn’t say I had a stretch like this that just went on and on for years. This feels tied to that time period, and it’s been pretty continuous since then, but not for two years or more.
During these seven months, has there been any time—even a few days or a week—when your mood improved significantly and you felt more like your usual self?

Not really, no. I mean, there might have been individual moments where I was distracted or got through a day a little easier, but I wouldn’t say there’s been a real stretch where I felt like myself again.

It’s been pretty much going on for about seven months now, since my husband stopped working after the downsizing. That’s kind of the marker in my mind, because before that things weren’t perfect, but I didn’t feel like this every day. Since then, it’s felt pretty continuous. I keep thinking maybe I’ll wake up and it’ll have lifted a little, but I don’t think I’ve had even a few days where I’d say my mood significantly improved.
During these seven months, have there been even a few days in a row where you felt noticeably better and more like your usual self, even if it didn't last?

Not that I can really point to, no. I’ve been trying to think of it in chunks, like whether there was a weekend or a few days where I woke up and thought, “Okay, I’m back to myself,” but it hasn’t been like that.

It’s been going on about seven months now, basically since my husband stopped working after the downsizing. That’s when I feel like everything sort of shifted, and since then I might have moments where I’m a little distracted or I get through something, but I wouldn’t call it a noticeable improvement for a few days in a row. It’s more like the same thing is still there underneath.
Have you noticed even a single day during these seven months where your mood felt noticeably better, even if just for a few hours or part of a day?

I mean… I’ve maybe had hours where I was busy enough not to think about it as much, but I wouldn’t call it noticeably better, exactly. It’s more like I got through that part of the day.

The overall thing has been going on for about seven months now, since my husband stopped working after the downsizing, and I keep using that as the dividing line in my head. Since then, even if there’s a small break in how much I’m focusing on it, it doesn’t feel like my mood actually lifts in a real way. It’s just… still there.
During these seven months, have you noticed even a single day where your mood felt significantly better, even if only for a short time?

I know I’ve kind of circled around this already, but no, not in the way you mean. I can’t think of a single day where I would say my mood was significantly better, even for a short time.

This has really been going on for about seven months, since my husband stopped working after the downsizing. That’s the point I keep coming back to, because before that I could still have normal ups and downs, but since then it’s felt like the same heaviness has just stayed there. There may have been moments where I was occupied or where I wasn’t actively thinking about it every second, but I wouldn’t describe that as my mood actually improving. It’s more like I was just distracted from it for a bit.
